simple.meaning: מָשָׁה (mâshâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to pull out (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Exodus, 2 Samuel, Psalms, beginning at Exodus 2:10. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָשָׁה (H4871) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָשָׁה (mâshâh) / H4871 is traced through Exodus 2:10, 2 Samuel 22:17, Psalms 18:17 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4871. mashah [ מָשָׁה ] verb draw (Arabic cleanse uterus of camel, Aramaic clean, stroke, the face, etc.; מְשָׁא (Talmud) wash the hands; Zinjirli משׂי [ י ] perhaps wash oneself, DHM Sendsch. 60 ); — Qal Perfect suffix מְשִׁיתִהוּ מִןהַֿמַּיִם Exod 2:10 out of the water I drew him (used to explain משֶׁה , but see this below) Hiph`il Imperfect suffix = Qal , figurative רַבִּים מִמַיִם יַמְשֵׁנִי 2Sam 22:17 = Psa 18:7 (subject ׳י ).

occurrences.englishText: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses,* “Moses” sounds like the Hebrew for “draw out”. and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
He sent from on high and he took me.
He delivered me from my strong enemy,
